chill.title: Read at the Swan House Gardens at Atlanta History Center
chill.description: The formal gardens behind the 1928 Swan House on the Atlanta History Center grounds are open during museum hours and offer the kind of structured, shaded green space that rewards a book and a slow afternoon.
chill.bonus: Bring a physical book — no phone, no podcasts — and finish at least 50 pages before you leave.

chill.title: Solo Afternoon at Callanwolde Fine Arts Center
chill.description: This 1920 Gothic Tudor estate in Druid Hills runs public gallery hours and open courtyard access that make wandering through its art-filled rooms and grounds feel like stumbling into a secret.
chill.bonus: Find the most obscure corner of the building and sit in silence there for five minutes before leaving.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Jimmy Carter Presidential Library Gardens
chill.description: The Japanese-inspired garden and reflection pool surrounding the Carter Center is one of Atlanta's most quietly beautiful public spaces and almost no one treats it like the destination it is.
chill.bonus: Sit on a bench, put your phone face-down, and stay completely still for ten full minutes.

chill.title: Sunset at Kennesaw Mountain Battlefield
chill.description: The wide open summit of Kennesaw Mountain delivers a panoramic Atlanta skyline sunset above Civil War earthworks that most Atlantans have never actually climbed to.
chill.bonus: Stay on the summit until you can see the first city lights switch on across the skyline before heading down.

chill.title: Coffee and Records at Wax 'n' Facts in Little Five Points
chill.description: Open since 1976, this cramped, floor-to-ceiling vinyl shop in Little Five Points is staffed by people who will change what you think you know about music.
chill.bonus: Describe a feeling, not a genre, to the staff and let them pick a record for you to buy cold.

chill.title: Evening at Fernbank Museum of Natural History
chill.description: The 'Fernbank After Dark' series turns the world's largest dinosaurs under the same roof as craft cocktails into one of Atlanta's most unexpectedly great date nights.
chill.bonus: Stand directly under the Argentinosaurus skeleton and take a photo looking straight up — the scale is disorienting in the best way.

chill.title: Browse Charis Books & More in Candler Park
chill.description: America's oldest feminist bookstore is a genuine neighborhood institution where the staff picks are always better than any algorithm and the community board tells the real story of Atlanta.
chill.bonus: Buy one book chosen entirely by the staff — no peeking at reviews first.

chill.title: Piedmont Park Afternoon Drift
chill.description: Piedmont Park has been Atlanta's backyard since 1904, and on any given afternoon it's the city's best cross-section — runners, picnics, skyline views, and pickup soccer all at once.
chill.bonus: Join whatever pickup game is happening — soccer, frisbee, volleyball — for at least fifteen minutes.

chill.title: Rooftop Sunset at Ponce City Market's Skyline Park
chill.description: Ride the elevator up to Skyline Park for mini-golf, games, and a wraparound sunset view over the Atlanta skyline.
chill.bonus: Stay until the skyline lights actually turn on

chill.title: Slow Afternoon at the High Museum of Art
chill.description: Wander the High Museum's light-filled galleries at your own pace, no itinerary required.
chill.bonus: Pick your favorite piece and explain why to a stranger nearby

chill.title: Slow Walk Down the Beltline Eastside Trail at Golden Hour
chill.description: Stroll the Eastside Trail as the light goes gold, past murals, patios, and the Historic Fourth Ward Park pond.
chill.bonus: Take the long way and detour through Historic Fourth Ward Park

chill.title: Wander the Atlanta Botanical Garden
chill.description: Lose an afternoon among the orchid house, canopy walk, and skyline views inside Midtown's Atlanta Botanical Garden.
chill.bonus: Find the plant with the strangest name and look up why it's called that

social.title: Late Jazz at Cafe 290
social.description: This Sandy Springs jazz room has been hosting serious live jazz since 1980 and draws performers who treat a Tuesday night residency with the same weight as a major venue.
social.bonus: Stay for both sets, tip heavy after the first, and introduce yourself to the bandleader at the break.

social.title: Comedy Night at Dad's Garage Theatre
social.description: Inman Park's improv institution has been producing sharp, unpredictable comedy since 1995 and packs its weekend shows with material you will absolutely not see coming.
social.bonus: Volunteer if the performers ask for an audience member — no hesitating, hand up immediately.

social.title: Beer Tasting at Monday Night Garage
social.description: Monday Night Brewing's West Midtown taproom is the larger, wilder sibling to the original and pours a rotating lineup of experimental beers in a space that's equal parts warehouse and playground.
social.bonus: Order the most unusual thing on the board — no settling for the easy IPA.

social.title: Sunday Gospel Brunch at Paschal's
social.description: Paschal's has been feeding Atlanta's civil rights leaders and Sunday churchgoers since 1947, and the weekend brunch with live gospel music is as close as the city gets to a sacred ritual.
social.bonus: Strike up a real conversation with the table next to you — not small talk, actual conversation.

social.title: Pinball at Joystick Gamebar
social.description: This Edgewood Avenue bar stocks wall-to-wall vintage arcade machines and pinball tables, and the combination of cheap beer and genuine competition makes it one of the most reliably fun nights in the city.
social.bonus: Challenge a stranger to best-of-three on any machine — loser buys the next round.

social.title: Friday Night at MJQ Concourse
social.description: Atlanta's longest-running underground dance bar beneath a parking deck has been pouring cheap drinks and spinning good music since 1994, and it still hits exactly the same.
social.bonus: Stay until 2am without checking your phone — no excuses, no peeking.

social.title: Cocktail Tasting at Ticonderoga Club
social.description: This Krog Street Market bar is one of the most precise cocktail programs in the South, run by bartenders who treat every drink like it matters because they actually believe it does.
social.bonus: Order blind — ask the bartender to make you something they're personally proud of, no parameters.

social.title: Night Out at Sister Louisa's Church
social.description: Part dive bar, part outsider-art installation, part Sunday school fever dream — this Edgewood Avenue fixture is the most Atlanta bar in Atlanta and has been for over a decade.
social.bonus: Find the most irreverent piece of art on the wall, photograph it, and send it to someone religious in your contacts.

social.title: Live Music at Variety Playhouse
social.description: Little Five Points' 1,000-capacity jewel has hosted everyone from Norah Jones to Outkast and remains the gold standard for mid-size live music in the South.
social.bonus: Get to the rail before the opener starts and don't leave it all night.

social.title: Late Night at Clermont Lounge
social.description: Atlanta's oldest strip club, open since 1965 in the basement of the Clermont Hotel, is a singular institution where the drinks are stiff, the crowd is everyone, and Blondie still crushes beer cans.
social.bonus: Buy Blondie a beer, tip heavy, and stay for at least two of her sets — no phones.

social.title: Stand-Up Night at The Punchline Comedy Club
social.description: Grab a two-drink minimum and a table at Atlanta's longest-running comedy club for a lineup of touring headliners.
social.bonus: Sit in the first three rows instead of hiding in the back

social.title: Trivia Night at Wood's Chapel BBQ
social.description: Grab a table, order the brisket, and put your team's random knowledge to the test at weekly trivia.
social.bonus: Let the least confident person on your team answer the final question

social.title: Catch a Braves Game at Truist Park
social.description: Get loud in the outfield seats and stick around The Battery for drinks after the last out.
social.bonus: Buy a stranger sitting near you a beer

social.title: Group Walk-and-Talk on the Beltline with Coffee Stops
social.description: Round up friends for a walking loop of the Eastside Trail with a coffee or espresso martini stop along the way.
social.bonus: Invite one person you haven't hung out with one-on-one before

active.title: Twilight Round at Bobby Jones Golf Course
active.description: Atlanta's beloved public course in Buckhead has been host to locals since 1932 and offers walk-up twilight tee times that make a spontaneous nine holes completely doable.
active.bonus: Play the back nine with no rangefinder — trust your eyes and commit to every club choice.

active.title: Stand-Up Paddleboard at Lake Allatoona
active.description: An hour north of the city, Lake Allatoona opens up into quiet coves perfect for a SUP session that feels nothing like Atlanta and everything like an escape.
active.bonus: Paddle to an empty cove, anchor yourself, and jump in — no ladder, no steps.

active.title: Morning Hike at Panola Mountain State Park
active.description: This 100-acre granite monadnock southeast of the city offers a legitimately wild trail experience with rare plant communities and zero crowds before 9am.
active.bonus: Make it to the bare granite summit rock and eat your breakfast up there.

active.title: Climb at Stone Summit Midtown
active.description: Atlanta's flagship climbing gym inside a converted warehouse on Marietta Street has 30,000 square feet of walls that will humble you regardless of your experience level.
active.bonus: Flash a V3 bouldering problem on your first try — no previewing other people's beta.

active.title: Cycle the Beltline Westside Trail
active.description: The Westside Trail cuts through one of Atlanta's fastest-evolving neighborhoods — rent a Relay bike and cover four miles of fresh pavement past murals, community gardens, and the real working city.
active.bonus: Stop at every major mural, photograph them all, and post the series as a single story before you finish the trail.

active.title: Run the Silver Comet Trail from Mavell Road
active.description: Atlanta's smoothest, most traffic-free long run starts at the Mavell Road trailhead and unspools west through quiet Cobb County on a former railroad grade.
active.bonus: Run at least six miles out before turning back — the trail only gets better the further you go.

active.title: Bouldering Session at Stone Summit Climbing Gym
active.description: Chalk up and work the bouldering walls at one of the largest climbing gyms in the Southeast.
active.bonus: Try a route two grades harder than your comfort level

active.title: Rent a Bike and Ride the Beltline Loop
active.description: Rent a bike and knock out a full loop of the Atlanta Beltline's Eastside and Westside trails in one ride.
active.bonus: Stop at a mural you've never seen and take a photo next to it

active.title: Pickup Pickleball at Piedmont Park Courts
active.description: Show up to Piedmont Park's courts, find an open game, and get looped into a round of pickleball with strangers.
active.bonus: Play a game with whoever's next in line instead of your own group

active.title: Kayak the Chattahoochee at Azalea Park
active.description: Put in at Azalea Park and paddle a stretch of Class I water through the Chattahoochee's tree-lined banks.
active.bonus: Swap paddling positions with someone halfway through

foodie.title: Soul Food at Busy Bee Cafe
foodie.description: Since 1947, this Sweet Auburn institution has fed civil rights leaders, mayors, and anyone who knows where Atlanta's real soul food lives.
foodie.bonus: Ask the staff about the restaurant's civil rights history — there's a story attached to almost every table.

foodie.title: Cocktails at Paper Crane
foodie.description: Intimate, low-lit, and technically precise, this Midtown cocktail bar rewards anyone willing to skip the obvious rooftop and drink something genuinely well-made.
foodie.bonus: Tell the bartender your mood in one word and let them build you something off-menu.

foodie.title: Ethiopian Feast at Desta Ethiopian Kitchen
foodie.description: Desta brings proper Addis Ababa-style injera and wot to Buckhead in a warm, family-run room that fills up fast and stays full for good reason.
foodie.bonus: Order the combination platter for two, eat it entirely without utensils, and finish every drop of injera.

foodie.title: Pizza at Antico Pizza Napoletana
foodie.description: Standing-room-only, wood-fired, and brutally authentic — Antico's communal tables and Neapolitan pies have made this Home Park spot a genuine Atlanta legend.
foodie.bonus: Share your table with a stranger and swap a slice — it's expected here.

foodie.title: Tacos at Buford Highway Taqueria
foodie.description: The stretch of Buford Highway that feeds Atlanta's soul — this no-frills counter serves birria and lengua tacos that locals will drive across town for.
foodie.bonus: Order one taco you've never eaten before by pointing at it on the board without asking what it is first.

foodie.title: Dinner at Staplehouse
foodie.description: One of Atlanta's most quietly celebrated restaurants turns seasonal ingredients into plates that feel both restrained and thrilling in equal measure.
foodie.bonus: Tell the server it's your first visit and ask them to choose one dish for you that isn't on the printed menu.

foodie.title: Lunch at Mary Mac's Tea Room
foodie.description: Atlanta's oldest continually operating restaurant serves the definitive Southern lunch — fried chicken, pot likker, and cornbread that hasn't changed since 1945.
foodie.bonus: Order the pot likker and drink it straight from the bowl the way regulars do.

foodie.title: Breakfast at The Varsity
foodie.description: The world's largest drive-in, open since 1928, runs on controlled chaos — and a chili dog with a Frosted Orange at 8am is as Atlanta as it gets.
foodie.bonus: Order by mimicking exactly how the counter staff shouts — 'What'll ya have?' — and don't break character.

foodie.title: Dinner at The Colonnade Restaurant
foodie.description: Open since 1927, The Colonnade serves the definitive Atlanta Sunday-supper plate — fried chicken, creamed corn, and yeast rolls — in a dining room that hasn't needed to change a thing.
foodie.bonus: Order the full fried chicken dinner and finish every side — ask your server which one most people leave behind.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Bacchanalia
foodie.description: Settle in for Anne Quatrano's celebrated seasonal tasting menu, one of Atlanta's most decorated fine-dining rooms.
foodie.bonus: Let the sommelier pick your pairing instead of choosing yourself

foodie.title: Buford Highway International Food Tour
foodie.description: Drive the strip malls of Buford Highway for some of the best Vietnamese, Korean, and Chinese food in the Southeast, starting with pho at Nam Phuong.
foodie.bonus: Order something you've never heard of off the menu

foodie.title: Browse the Vendors at Krog Street Market
foodie.description: Wander this Inman Park food hall for wood-fired pizza, fresh oysters, and a scoop of small-batch ice cream to finish.
foodie.bonus: Split three different dishes with whoever you're with instead of ordering your own

foodie.title: Food Hall Crawl at Ponce City Market
foodie.description: Work your way through a dozen vendors under one roof at Ponce City Market's Central Food Hall, from ramen to fried chicken.
foodie.bonus: Order the one dish on the menu you can't pronounce

adventure.title: Oakland Cemetery Self-Guided Walk
adventure.description: Founded in 1850, Oakland Cemetery holds six mayors, a golf legend, and a corner of the Civil War dead — and it's the most peaceful 88 acres in all of Atlanta.
adventure.bonus: Find Margaret Mitchell's grave and leave something — a flower, a note, a coin — before you go.

adventure.title: Explore Krog Street Tunnel
adventure.description: Krog Street Tunnel is Atlanta's living gallery — a legal graffiti corridor that changes constantly and marks the seam between Inman Park and Cabbagetown.
adventure.bonus: Leave your mark — even if it's just a chalk outline of your hand on the wall.

adventure.title: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historic Site
adventure.description: Sweet Auburn's two-block stretch holds MLK's birth home, Ebenezer Baptist Church, and his tomb — a pilgrimage that recalibrates your sense of what one city block can mean to history.
adventure.bonus: Sit alone in a pew at Ebenezer Baptist for ten minutes of silence before you leave.

adventure.title: Zip-line at Treetop Quest Fowler Park
adventure.description: Treetop Quest's aerial obstacle course threads through the forest canopy north of the city and gives your grip strength and your nerve a real audit.
adventure.bonus: Take the highest course available — no skipping elements, no looking down more than once.

adventure.title: Georgia Aquarium Whale Shark Tank
adventure.description: The world's largest aquarium puts you face-to-face with whale sharks in a tank so vast it feels like standing at the edge of the open ocean.
adventure.bonus: Find a spot at the main viewing window and stay perfectly still for five full minutes — let the fish come to you.

adventure.title: Trap Music Museum
adventure.description: T.I.'s immersive shrine to Atlanta trap culture puts you inside the genre's DNA through original artifacts, studio recreations, and rooms that hit harder than any playlist.
adventure.bonus: Record a freestyle in the booth installation and post it unedited — no takes back.

adventure.title: Beltline Eastside Trail at Night
adventure.description: The Eastside Trail transforms after dark into a lit social corridor where the whole city — skaters, cyclists, dog walkers — moves together through Inman Park and Ponce City.
adventure.bonus: Stop a stranger, ask them their favorite Atlanta hidden gem, and actually go find it before the week is out.

adventure.title: Float the Hooch on a Chattahoochee Tube Run
adventure.description: Grab an inner tube and drift the Chattahoochee River's Discovery Unit for a lazy, cold-water float on a hot Atlanta afternoon.
adventure.bonus: Bring a waterproof speaker and share the aux

adventure.title: Climb Kennesaw Mountain's Summit Trail
adventure.description: Hike the steep paved trail up Kennesaw Mountain to a Civil War battlefield summit with sweeping views of the Atlanta skyline.
adventure.bonus: Read one historical marker out loud to whoever you're with

adventure.title: Zip the Canopy Tour at Historic Banning Mills
adventure.description: Soar across the longest zip line course in North America through the Georgia treetops at the world's largest canopy tour.
adventure.bonus: Take the night zip line option if it's offered that day

adventure.title: Hike Stone Mountain's Walk-Up Trail at Sunrise
adventure.description: Beat the crowds and climb Stone Mountain's granite face before the sun clears the treeline for a 360° view over the city.
adventure.bonus: Skip the skyride — walk up both ways
